references.text: Isaiah describes similar spiritual blindness where the people grope along the wall like the blind and stumble in broad daylight as if it were twilight.
Job describes how the wicked meet darkness during the day and grope at noon as though it were night.
Zephaniah prophesies that people will walk like the blind because they have sinned against the Lord.
Isaiah describes a people who are plundered and exploited, trapped in caves and hidden in prisons, with no one to rescue them.
Judges tells how the Lord's anger came upon Israel so that they were handed over to plunderers and oppressors, unable to resist their enemies.
The same chapter in Deuteronomy describes oppression where a foreign people will eat the fruit of their labor, leaving them only oppressed and crushed.
The psalmist prays that the eyes of the enemies be darkened so they cannot see, a curse that mirrors the blindness described in Deuteronomy.
The Amalekites and Canaanites struck down the Israelites and drove them back, an example of how they had no success on their paths.
